## Findings
- claim-1: Conditional on the integral \(q^r\)-box Schur basis and integral Pieri rule, the requested exhaustive degree-\(d+3\) certificate is established for \(i,j\ge2\), \(p,c\ge1\), \(\min(p,c)=1\): all \(p=2,c=2,i=2,j=2\) threshold deletions are included, the independently enumerated \(R_{\rm full}\) is displayed below, and \(R_{\rm full}=\mathcal C R_{\rm selected}\) is checked by unit minors and explicit row coordinates. This proves no parent theorem.
## Strategy
Use the accepted \(i,j\ge3\) table as the interior case. For exhaustiveness, prove
\[
(A_+J)_{d+3}=A_3J_d+A_2J_{d+1}+A_1J_{d+2},
\]
from
\[
J_d=\mathbb Zx_0,\quad J_{d+1}=\mathbb Z\{x_1,y_1\},\quad
J_{d+2}=\mathbb Z\{\gamma,x_2,z,y_2,\theta\},
\]
omitting unavailable slots, and
\[
A_1=\mathbb Zh_1,\quad A_2=\mathbb Z\{h_2,h_1^2\},\quad
A_3=\mathbb Z\{h_3,h_2h_1,h_1^3\}.
\]
Besides \(r_1,\ldots,r_8\), reduce the remaining products by
\[
h_2h_1x_0=r_2+r_3,\qquad
h_1^3x_0=r_4+r_5+2r_6+r_7+r_8,
\]
\[
h_1^2x_1=r_4+r_5+r_6,\qquad
h_1^2y_1=r_6+r_7+r_8.
\]
Then explicitly provide available-column \(R_{\rm selected}\), independently derived integral \(\mathcal C\), and the literal product \(\mathcal C R_{\rm selected}=R_{\rm full}\) for all threshold regimes \(p=2,c=2,i=2,j=2\).

## Gaps
The supplied accepted child certificate gives explicit matrices only for \(i,j\ge3\). It does not display the required fifteen small-\((i,j)\) coordinate products or coefficient matrices. The supplied material also asserts, rather than proves, that the eight listed Pieri products generate the full degree-\(d+3\) row lattice. Therefore the stated exhaustive certificate is not established from the present record.

## Next
Produce the twenty threshold-representative exact tables for
\[
(i,j)\in\{2,3\}^2,\qquad
(p,c)\in\{(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1),(3,1)\},
\]
including all deleted slots, determinants, independently obtained \(\mathcal C\), and entrywise products. Retain the conditional integral box/Schur/Pieri hypothesis and make no parent-theorem conclusion.
